title: Maximum Average Subarray I
description: Find the contiguous subarray of length k with the maximum average using a fixed-size sliding window.

data.text: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, find the contiguous subarray of length exactly `k` that has the maximum average value, and return that average.

**Input:** `nums = [1, 12, -5, -6, 50, 3]`, `k = 4`

**Output:** `12.75`

**Explanation:** The subarray `[12, -5, -6, 50]` has the maximum average `51 / 4 = 12.75`.
For each starting index, sum the next `k` elements. This is O(n·k) and re-adds the same values repeatedly.

data.title: Brute Force O(n·k)

data.text: Each window differs from the previous one by exactly two elements: the element leaving on the left and the element entering on the right. Keep a running sum and adjust it, giving O(n).

data.title: Sliding Window O(n)
data.content: Add the incoming element, subtract the outgoing one.

data.title: Keep the sum as a long
data.text: Summing `k` values up to 10,000 can overflow a 32-bit `int` when `n` is large. Accumulate in `long` and divide by `k` only at the end — dividing early loses precision.

data.caption: A fixed-size window slides one position at a time: one element leaves at the left, one enters at the right.

data.title: Complete solution
data.content: Fixed-size windows always cost exactly two updates per slide, so the window sum is maintained in constant time. This same template solves 'find all anagrams in a string' and 'maximum points you can obtain from cards'.
